issuer: the Island Traffic Authority (the licence is paid for at Tax Administration Jamaica)
note: The Road Traffic Act, 2018 (in force since 1 February 2023), on the Houses of Parliament's site, read 2026-10-31: s. 26(1)(e), the Authority shall not grant a driver's licence unless the applicant is at least seventeen and one-half years of age (and has held a learner's permit for at least six months, s. 26(1)(a)); s. 2(2)(b), a Class B licence entitles its holder to drive motor cars not for reward; s. 25(2)(a), a licence remains in force five years. The age is the Act's own words, 17 years and 6 months. Tax Administration Jamaica's Rates and Fees page, read again 2026-10-31: Private Driver's Licence $5,400.00, held as the Class B licence's fee (TAJ's page names the licence by its old name, private; a reading). The Act's first year of zero alcohol (s. 27(2)) isn't a separate licence and isn't held. TAJ issues no identity card. Until 2026-10-31 Jamaica stood blocked because the age falls between birthdays.
